treatyPosition.currentStance: The United States supports a global plastics agreement but has historically opposed binding caps on primary plastic polymer production, favoring national flexibility and a focus on waste management, product design, and recycling infrastructure.
treatyPosition.inc52Position: At INC-5.2 in Geneva (August 2025), the United States did not join the High Ambition Coalition's call for a binding cap on virgin plastic production. The session adjourned without a final treaty text. User: confirm exact US delegation statement before publishing.

historicalRounds.position: Engaged in negotiations; declined to support a binding production cap; emphasized national circumstances and downstream measures.

domesticPolicies.name: Save Our Seas 2.0 Act
domesticPolicies.summary: Federal law strengthening US marine debris response, expanding the Marine Debris Foundation, and authorizing investment in domestic recycling infrastructure and international partnerships to address plastic pollution.

domesticPolicies.name: California SB 54 — Plastic Pollution Prevention and Packaging Producer Responsibility Act
domesticPolicies.summary: Landmark state-level EPR law requiring producers of single-use packaging and plastic foodware to ensure all such material sold in California is recyclable or compostable by 2032, with phased reductions in single-use plastic packaging and a producer-funded mitigation fund.
